DAMAGE CAUSE: Deliberate cutting by a state actor
ROUTE REDUNDANCY: Multiple cables on the same corridor
DETECTION AND LOCATION: Traffic monitoring at the landing station

Fishing trawl or anchor.requires: a vessel working over the cable route
Fishing trawl or anchor.provides: shallow water damage, an identifiable vessel track, the commonest cause by far

Submarine landslide.provides: multiple cables cut simultaneously, deep water, no responsible party

Deliberate cutting by a state actor.requires: a vessel or vehicle capable of reaching the cable
Deliberate cutting by a state actor.provides: precise simultaneous cuts, deniability, no accidental signature

Equipment failure in a repeater.requires: an electronic fault in the wet plant
Equipment failure in a repeater.provides: no physical break in the cable, capacity lost on some fibres only

Single cable serving the territory.provides: total loss of connectivity on any break, no alternative at all

Multiple cables on the same corridor.requires: several cables sharing a seabed route
Multiple cables on the same corridor.provides: apparent redundancy, common-mode failure from one seabed event

Geographically diverse cables.requires: paths separated by hundreds of kilometres
Geographically diverse cables.provides: genuine redundancy against any local event

Satellite backup available.provides: continuity of essential traffic, a small fraction of cable capacity

Optical time-domain reflectometry.requires: access to the fibre from a landing station
Optical time-domain reflectometry.provides: distance to the fault along the cable, no cause information

Traffic monitoring at the landing statio.provides: immediate awareness of loss, no location

Vessel tracking correlation.provides: identification of a vessel over the fault at the time, only for surface vessels

Repair ship survey.provides: definitive location and cause, days to weeks to arrive
